claim: Prediction-error curiosity (ICM, RND, disagreement) gives large gains over no-bonus agents in sparse-reward settings such as VizDoom sparse (ICM+A3C 100% vs TRPO 26.0%, A3C 0.0%) and Montezuma (RND finds more than half the rooms, mean 7,570 to 10,070).
agent_test: Add a curiosity bonus to branch choice in a scaffold run versus uniform branch choice, equal total tokens on sparse-answer puzzles.

claim: Raw prediction error is exploitable by unlearnable noise: a noisy TV slows both inverse-dynamics and random-feature curious agents, though long runs sometimes recover.
agent_test: Insert an unanswerable-but-novel subtask; measure the share of tokens spent on it by error-driven vs progress-driven selection.

claim: Learning progress (error decrease) is the designed fix: it ignores both mastered and unlearnable regions; the zone robot avoids the noise zone throughout.
agent_test: Rank subproblems by recent drop in verifier error rather than by error; compare at equal tokens.

claim: Learning-progress curricula beat random and sometimes hand-built oracle curricula: ALP-GMM 14.9% vs RIAC 8.6% on short walkers, 80% vs oracle 68% on Hexagon Tracks, CURIOUS recovers 95% performance 45% faster after perturbation.
agent_test: Schedule a task set by absolute LP versus random order across an agent session; compare final solved fraction.

claim: Bonus-based exploration did not beat epsilon-greedy in a controlled Rainbow Atari replication; pseudo-counts did worse on easy games except Seaquest; RND and ICM only matched.
schema_part: G (do not assume curiosity always helps)
agent_test: Include an epsilon-greedy-style random-branch control in every curiosity ablation.

claim: Prediction-error bonuses are fragile under stochasticity: sticky actions cut BYOL-Explore rooms about 25% and returns about 75% on Montezuma; hindsight variants repair this.
agent_test: Add noise to the verifier signal and check whether the branch ranker degrades.

claim: Episodic reachability novelty gives much more than ICM in visually rich sparse tasks: DMLab Very Sparse PPO 8.6, ICM 11.2, EC 24.7, ECO 40.5; dense tasks unchanged.
agent_test: Use within-episode novelty against own earlier attempts as a repeat-detection rule.

claim: An LLM can act as the interestingness model: OMNI learns 82 Crafter tasks vs 55 for LP (success 0.56 vs 0.42); differences vs oracle interestingness mostly not significant.
agent_test: Let the scaffold LLM rate subgoal interest and compare to a progress-based ranker at equal tokens.

claim: LLM-proposed goals are mostly sensible but not always: ELLM goals 64.9% good, 5% not allowed, 13.6% context-insensitive, 16.4% common-sense violating; ELLM unlocks about 6 vs oracle 9 achievements.
agent_test: Filter self-proposed subgoals with a cheap check; count the rejected share.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: A prompt-only automatic curriculum is strong: Voyager gets 3.3x unique items, tech-tree levels up to 15.3x faster, 2.3x distance; a random curriculum drops items 93%.
agent_test: Ablate the self-curriculum in a long-horizon LLM task with a random-order control.

claim: Motif shows LLM preferences can be turned into intrinsic reward that solves sparse NetHack tasks where extrinsic-only and RND scored 0, but behaviour can be steered (+106% gold) and misaligned.
agent_test: Check that an LLM-derived progress signal does not reward proxy behaviour: audit final answers.

claim: Curiosity bonuses help LLM reasoning RL modestly: CDE on Qwen3-4B-Base raises GRPO average 48.2 to 50.6 and AIME24 Avg@16 20.8 to 23.3.
agent_test: Not testable without training; scaffold analog is perplexity-driven sampling.

claim: MAGELLAN predicts learning progress for unseen goals with LLM embeddings (held-out competence error 0.11 vs 0.53 for online ALP) and is the only method fully mastering a large evolving goal space.
agent_test: Predict which problem types are learnable from past runs and route tokens accordingly.

claim: Knowledge-based intrinsic motivation needs a model of the environment, so a prompt-only agent can use it only through an explicit predictor (a stated expectation compared with the outcome).
agent_test: Make the agent state a prediction before each probe and score its surprise.

claim: Infants allocate attention by learning progress more than by surprise or predictability (Poli 2020: Wald chi2 48.87 vs 19.38 and 21.87, 43 infants), and look away from events that are too predictable or too surprising (Kidd 2012: 42 and 30 infants, Goldilocks near 1.25 bits). No independent replication was found.
schema_part: O2 (selection by progress, not by raw surprise)
agent_test: Choose the next subproblem by recent drop in verifier error versus by current error; compare tokens to solve.

claim: In one code base (Hou 2025), a learning-progress reward kept state coverage under noise (MiniWorld 1,347.6 average states; Atari drops 3.9 and 4.7 percent) while ICM, RND, ensemble and episodic baselines degraded; on the clean maze EDT was best. Same-agent head-to-head exists but only from the method's own authors.
agent_test: Run error-ranked and progress-ranked branch choice on a task set with unanswerable items; count tokens spent on them.

claim: Reasoning LLMs show a real noisy-TV failure: on questions with a missing premise they spend about 2x to 4x more tokens and cannot abstain, so an unanswerable item can drain a token budget unless a stop rule exists.
agent_test: Insert missing-premise subtasks into a scaffold run; measure token share with and without a no-progress stop rule.

claim: Verbal self-prediction in LLMs is weak without finetuning: Binder 2025 shows self-prediction accuracy near the majority-answer baseline for untrained models, 48.5% for finetuned Llama 70B, calibration error 23.0 falling to 8.7 after self-prediction training, and failure on long outputs. A stated-expectation surprise signal in a prompt-only agent is therefore unproven.
agent_test: Have the agent state a predicted verifier result before each step; measure calibration (Brier) of the statement.

claim: Founding experiments carry few numbers: Schmidhuber 2010 gives none for the 1991 systems; Oudeyer 2007 gives 85% time in the second zone after about 3000 steps, plateau error near 0.09, structured trajectory in 34% of 200 runs. Treat these as design precedents.
agent_test: none (background)

claim: No study was found that compares a learning-progress ranker with an error ranker for subproblem choice in a prompt-only LLM agent at equal tokens, tests noisy-TV traps in a scaffold, or accounts for curiosity token cost. These remain open.
agent_test: Run the head-to-head ourselves at equal total tokens.
